question: A 36-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital because of irritability, nausea, and diarrhea. She has a history of recreational oxycodone use and last took a dose 48 hours ago. Physical examination shows mydriasis, rhinorrhea, and piloerection. A drug is administered that provides an effect similar to oxycodone but does not cause euphoria. Which of the following best explains the difference in effect?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Oxycodone" -> "binds to opioid receptors in the brain" -> "causes euphoria" -> "relieves pain" -> "causes physical dependence" -> "leads to withdrawal symptoms upon cessation" -> "irritability, nausea, and diarrhea upon withdrawal" -> "mydriasis, rhinorrhea, and piloerection" -> "48 hours since last dose" -> "similar drug administered" -> "provides effect similar to oxycodone but no euphoria" -> "lower tolerance" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Oxycodone" -> "binds to opioid receptors in the brain" -> "causes euphoria" -> "relieves pain" -> "lower tolerance to the drug" -> "less euphoria experienced with similar drug" -> "lower tolerance" -> 75%
analysis: The drug administered provides a similar effect to oxycodone but does not cause euphoria, indicating it is likely a partial agonist or antagonist at the opioid receptors. The symptoms of mydriasis, rhinorrhea, and piloerection are consistent with opioid withdrawal. The difference in effect is likely due to the drug having lower efficacy compared to oxycodone.
